title: Garudhiya (Maldivian clear tuna broth)

ingredients.name: fresh tuna, cut into chunks, bones and head pieces included if possible
lime wedges, steamed rice and chilli to serve

steps: Rinse the tuna thoroughly in cold water.
Put it in a pot with the water and salt and bring slowly to a boil.
Skim off the foam that rises and keep skimming until the broth runs clear.
Add the curry leaves, onion and chillies if you like, and simmer gently for 20 to 25 minutes until the fish is fully cooked and firm.
Taste for salt and serve the fish and broth in bowls with steamed rice, lime and chilli.

title: Gulha (Maldivian fried tuna and coconut dumplings)
steps: Rub the flour, salt and the 2 tablespoons of oil together, then add enough warm water to form a smooth dough and rest it for 20 minutes.
Mash the tuna with the onion, coconut, chillies, turmeric, lime juice and curry leaves into a fairly dry filling.
Divide the dough into walnut-sized balls and flatten each into a small round.
Put a teaspoon of filling in the centre and pinch the dough closed around it, rolling it into a smooth ball.
Heat the frying oil to medium-hot and fry the balls in batches for 4 to 5 minutes until deep golden and crisp.
Drain on paper towels and serve warm with tea or chilli sauce.

title: Kandu Kukulhu (Maldivian tuna rolls in coconut curry)

ingredients.name: tuna loin, sliced into 8 thin strips
kitchen string, to tie the rolls (a strip of coconut leaf is traditional)

steps: Heat the coconut oil and fry the onion, garlic and chillies until golden.
Add the grated coconut and curry leaves and cook until the coconut turns golden brown.
Stir in the curry powder, cumin and salt and cook for about 5 minutes into a thick paste, then cool it.
Spread some paste on each tuna strip, roll it up and tie it with string.
Put the rolls in a pan with the coconut milk and any remaining paste and simmer very gently for 10 to 12 minutes, turning once, until the tuna is cooked through.
Remove the string and serve with rice or roshi.

title: Mas Huni (Maldivian tuna, coconut and onion breakfast)

ingredients.name: (about 160 g each) tuna in water or brine, drained
roshi or other flatbread, to serve

steps: Flake the drained tuna finely into a bowl.
If using desiccated coconut, moisten it with a spoonful of warm water and let it soften for 5 minutes.
Add the coconut, onion and chillies to the tuna.
Squeeze in the lime juice, add salt and mix well with your fingertips until the mixture is moist and evenly combined.
Serve at once with warm roshi and sweet tea.

title: Mas Riha (Maldivian tuna curry with coconut milk)
steps: Heat the oil and fry the onions until golden brown.
Add the garlic, ginger, chillies and curry leaves and fry for 2 minutes.
Stir in the curry powder, turmeric and salt, then add the tuna and coat it with the spices.
Pour in the water, cover and simmer on low heat for 10 minutes.
Add the coconut milk and cook gently for 5 minutes more, without letting it boil hard, then stir in the lime juice.
Serve hot with rice or roshi.

title: Miruhulee Boava (Maldivian octopus curry)
steps: Put the octopus in a pot with the water and salt, bring to a simmer, cover and cook for 30 to 40 minutes until the thickest part is nearly tender, then cut it into bite-sized pieces and keep the cooking liquid.
Heat the coconut oil in a clean pot and fry the onions until golden.
Add the garlic, chillies, curry leaves, cloves and pepper and fry for 2 minutes.
Add the octopus and about 150 ml of its cooking liquid and mix well.
Cover and simmer for 15 to 20 minutes, until the octopus is tender and the sauce is thick and clings to it.
Taste for salt and serve hot with rice or roshi.
